models.label: Linear model
concerns: Scores are unweighted: they describe these rows, not the population the survey weights stand for.

versus_baseline.tolerance_basis: Better only when the gain's 95% interval lies above zero and the gain is at least 1% of the baseline's log loss, 0.0062 here (a McFadden R² of 0.01, a convention): a gain above 0.0435. The interval is corrected for the 50 folds sharing training rows (Nadeau & Bengio 2003).

calibration.smoother: lowess, span 2/3, no robustness iterations (as rms val.prob)

internal_external.spread: Across 4 levels of site, log loss ranged from 0.444 to 0.560; the random−effects summary is 0.511 (95% CI 0.452 to 0.571), and a new site would score between 0.306 and 0.717 (95% prediction interval).

models.performance: Cross-validated log loss 0.515 (95% interval 0.467 to 0.563) by 5-fold cross-validation: the expected performance of this modeling procedure at this sample size.

models.performance: Cross-validated log loss 0.514 (95% interval 0.469 to 0.559) by 5-fold cross-validation: the expected performance of this modeling procedure at this sample size.

fit.cv_definition: Cross-validated scores are the mean over folds; the fold values show the spread.

selection.text: Choosing the best of 2 families by cross-validated log loss flatters the winner: Ridge's CV log loss of 0.514 is low by about 0.000285; corrected for the choice, 0.514 (95% interval 0.452 to 0.58) is the expected performance of this modeling procedure at this sample size (bootstrap bias-corrected cross-validation (Tsamardinos et al. 2018), 1,000 resamples of the out-of-fold predictions). The held-out score of a family declared before the seal is opened carries no such optimism.

fit.se_definition: Each standard error counts which rows were scored, with each fold's model as fitted (LeDell et al. 2015; DeLong's for the AUC); it leaves out how the models would vary with other training rows.

comparisons.sentence: Linear model against Ridge: log loss differs by 0.000 (95% interval of the difference −0.006 to 0.006; corrected repeated k-fold t −0.07 on 49 df, 10 × 5 folds): not distinguishable on these rows.

fit.precision: On these 480 training rows the cross-validated log loss has a standard error of 0.025 for Linear model and 0.023 for Ridge; whether two families differ is read from their paired interval, not from either one alone.
fit.imbalance: The event, `yes`, is 31% of the training rows. No resampling (SMOTE, over- or undersampling) or class weighting was applied: customary in machine-learning papers, resampling overestimates the rarer class's probability without raising the AUC (van den Goorbergh et al. 2022); a decision moves the threshold instead.
fit.tension: AUC is the customary headline: it ranks risks without asking whether they are right (semi-proper), so the models were compared, chosen and declared on log loss, a strictly proper score (Van Calster et al., STRATOS TG6).

comparison.method: the corrected repeated k-fold t (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004)

fit.comparisons_note: Each pairwise interval is descriptive: none is corrected for how many pairs there are, and the choice among the families is corrected by bootstrap bias-corrected cross-validation instead.

result.sentence: The held-out rows score the final model, declared on cross-validation before they are opened; its held-out log loss will be the result.

chain.because: the outcome is a binary outcome
chain.then: the models were compared, chosen and declared on log loss, and AUC is reported as the customary headline
every family and the no-predictor baseline were compared on 5-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times (50 paired folds, 49 degrees of freedom)

chain.because: the grouping question named `site`, with 4 levels
chain.then: every family was also validated internal–externally by it: each level scored by models fit on the others, with the random-effects summary and the spread
the best family's score is corrected for the choice by BBC-CV

benchmark.label: Regression with splines (benchmark)

versus_baseline.tolerance_basis: Better only when the gain's 95% interval lies above zero and the gain is at least 1% of the baseline's log loss, 0.0062 here (a McFadden R² of 0.01, a convention): a gain above 0.0574. The interval is corrected for the 50 folds sharing training rows (Nadeau & Bengio 2003).

differences.sentence: Regression with splines (benchmark) against Linear model: log loss differs by 0.014 (95% interval of the difference −0.040 to 0.013; corrected repeated k-fold t −1.03 on 49 df, 10 × 5 folds): not distinguishable on these rows.

Regression with splines (benchmark) against Ridge: log loss differs by 0.014 (95% interval of the difference −0.042 to 0.015; corrected repeated k-fold t −0.98 on 49 df, 10 × 5 folds): not distinguishable on these rows.

benchmark.sentence: The regression-with-splines benchmark (every continuous predictor a restricted cubic spline, knots by Harrell's rule, on the same in-fold preprocessing) scored cross-validated log loss 0.528 on the families' 50 paired folds, better than the no-predictor baseline.

interpretable.text: No flexible family was fitted, so there is nothing for the interpretable model to cost or gain against.

decision_curve.sentence: Decision curve analysis of Ridge's out-of-fold risks over thresholds from 0.05 to 0.5: it beats treating everyone and no one from 0.05 to 0.5 (Vickers & Elkin 2006); at the threshold Youden's J chose in each training fold (median 0.370), the held-out sensitivity was 0.625, the specificity 0.756 and the net benefit 0.107 per row.

groups.note: Too few rows of one class to score this group (fewer than 5).

subgroups.note: Whether `visits`'s numbers are codes or amounts is not settled, so its groups wait on that answer: its levels as codes, its thirds as an amount.

ask.label: `visits` is a count or an amount (a slope; a unit's rows averaged)
`visits` holds codes for categories (one indicator per level; a unit's rows take their most frequent value)

shrinkage.label: Shrink the regression's coefficients by 0.909 (model updating)
shrinkage.sentence: As model updating, the regression's coefficients were multiplied by 0.909, the out-of-fold calibration slope (cross-validation), and its intercept re-estimated with the shrunk linear predictor as an offset (−1.820).

Decision curve analysis of Ridge's out-of-fold risks over thresholds from 0.05 to 0.5: it beats treating everyone and no one from 0.05 to 0.5 (Vickers & Elkin 2006); at the threshold Youden's J chose in each training fold (median 0.370), the held-out sensitivity was 0.625, the specificity 0.756 and the net benefit 0.107 per row.
